stories.w: Proposal 3 goes to voters on November 3 alongside Proposal 4, and it would write the right to organize and bargain collectively into the state constitution, protect union shop agreements, and make it hard for a future Legislature to roll labor protections back. stories.t: Retired goats find new employment as therapy animals
stories.w: Lauren Gitlin has retired the 53 goat milking herd at Villa Villekulla Farm in Barnard and is turning the place into a nonprofit sanctuary offering animal assisted therapy, after years of finding it harder to justify commercial production for animals she had bonded with. stories.t: Absent State Action, Vermont Towns Move to Block Data Centers
stories.w: Morristown has become the third Vermont community to block data centers, passing a two year moratorium on any high impact use drawing more than 10 megawatts, 57,600 gallons of water a day, 10 acres of pavement or 70 decibels of noise, after Royalton's five year ban and South Burlington's August zoning change barring centers over 20,000 square feet. stories.t: What qualifies as a seasonal home in Vermont? New tax raises questions
stories.w: Vermont has nearly 50,000 homes counted as seasonally vacant, 14% of the housing stock, and this year's education law raises taxes on the ones fit for year round living that are not the owner's primary residence, starting in 2030. stories.t: Venetian Soda Lounge in Burlington’s Soda Plant Is for Sale
stories.w: Justin Bunnell moved to Orlando in late August for his wife's job and is selling both the Venetian Cocktail & Soda Lounge and the Venetian Beverages brand, with the lounge for sale by word of mouth and staying open in the meantime. stories.t: Vermont Almanac, an annual compendium of Vermont life, is shutting down
stories.w: After six editions, the Vermont Almanac is done, its founders announcing in a newsletter that they will not open preorders for a seventh. stories.w: Two derelict dams on the Brewster River in Jeffersonville are coming out, the first this week and the second in about two weeks, in a Smugglers' Notch Resort project with the Vermont Natural Resources Council that reconnects roughly 10 miles of trout habitat. stories.t: Is Any Town Willing to Host a 100-Bed Homeless Shelter?
stories.w: CVOEO pulled its proposal for a 100 bed low barrier shelter at the former mattress store at 1717 Williston Road six days before South Burlington's September 8 council meeting, after city staff objected on strained services, crime and transportation grounds. stories.w: Seven Days' Art Hop guide profiles the SEABA Center, the 7,000 square foot space in the former ArtsRiot building at 400 Pine that the South End Arts + Business Association moved into last fall. stories.w: Today is the 25th anniversary, and Kevin O'Connor's first person column for VTDigger tells it from the Vermont side, through Rutland native Michael Rosen watching from a block and a half away, former Port Authority officer Norma Hardy, who later became Vermont's first Black female police chief, and Bishop Kenneth Angell, whose brother David died on the first plane. stories.w: Seven Days' long feature on maternity care traces how Springfield closed its labor and delivery unit in 2019, Copley closed in 2025, and nearly one in three Vermonters giving birth now lives outside the recommended 30 minute drive to hospital obstetric care. stories.t: In reversal, Brattleboro Memorial Hospital will keep its birth center open
stories.w: Brattleboro Memorial announced Thursday evening it will keep its birth center open after all, reversing a July decision to close it on December 31. stories.t: Vermont regulators finalize 5.5% rate increase for Green Mountain Power customers
stories.w: The Public Utility Commission approved a 5.5% increase for Green Mountain Power's more than 275,000 Vermont customers, down from the 7.5% the utility asked for, and it takes effect October 1. Regulators approved about $113 million of the $341 million in four year resilience spending GMP requested, and the utility says storms are the reason it needs the money. stories.w: Kingdom Creamery of Vermont, the largest supplier of Vermont made creemee mix, cut production to a limited basis after Border Patrol detained three of its migrant workers in late July, all three were deported, and more employees left out of fear. stories.w: Vermont announced the first $11.7 million of its $195 million in federal Rural Health Transformation money, with $9 million going to the Vermont Student Assistance Corporation for tuition benefits for healthcare students who commit to five years working in state and $2.7 million to three nursing homes and four teaching institutions for licensed nursing assistant training. stories.w: We ran the closing news last month, and the last day is now here. Ray's Seafood Market & Restaurant closes its Pine Crest Drive location in Essex Junction for good on Saturday at 7 PM after 74 years, so this weekend is the last chance for a lap. stories.t: Album Review: Lily Seabird, 'Lightspheres on Their Way'
stories.w: Seven Days reviews Burlington songwriter Lily Seabird's new album Lightspheres on Their Way, out last week on Lame-O Records, and hears a turn toward louder, Crazy Horse style distortion after 2021's Beside Myself and last year's Trash Mountain. The record is only partly on streaming, so the reviewer's advice is to buy a copy at a local record store, and she plays Foam Brewers on November 15.
